title: Astrid Moon Cattery
description: Answers about adopting a kitten from Astrid Moon Cattery: waitlist, reservations and deposits, health testing, pickup and payment.

sections.html:
Frequently Asked Questions

Everything we are asked most often about our kittens: the waitlist, reservations, health testing, pickup and payment.

Do you currently have kittens available?

Our availability changes frequently! Because many of our kittens are reserved during scheduled reservation periods, we may have kittens who are still growing but are not yet officially available for reservation. If we don't currently have the right kitten for you, you're welcome to join our free waitlist for upcoming litters and reservation opportunities. We can also discuss approximate wait times based on your preferences when you initially inquire. Please note that all kitten inquiries are handled through email so we're able to keep our conversations and important information organized in one place.

How does your waitlist work?

Our waitlist is completely free and is the best way to stay informed about upcoming kittens. There is no separate waitlist form. Simply let us know through email that you would like to be added to our waitlist, along with your general preferences. Due to social media policies, we are unable to provide waitlist information through social media and prefer to keep all kitten inquiries in one place through email. Because litter sizes, genders, colors, coat lengths, and personalities can never be completely predicted, joining our waitlist does not guarantee a particular kitten or exact timeframe.

How does the reservation process work?

Reservations typically open when kittens are around 8 weeks old, although they may occasionally take place a little sooner or later depending on the individual litter and how the kittens are developing. When reservations open, we begin contacting families on our waitlist with information, photos, and/or videos of available kittens. Reservations are handled on a first-come, first-served basis. Once the waitlist is contacted and reservations open, kittens are available to reserve based on the order in which families are ready to move forward. Once you've selected your kitten, you'll receive our sales agreement electronically through JotForm to review and sign. Your kitten is officially reserved once the signed agreement and $800 reservation deposit have been received.

Is the $800 reservation deposit refundable?

Our reservation deposits are non-refundable and are applied directly toward your kitten's $3,000 purchase price. Once a kitten is reserved, that kitten is removed from availability for other families, which is why we encourage everyone to make sure they're comfortable moving forward before submitting their deposit.

Can I request a specific gender, color, or coat length?

Absolutely! We're happy to note your preferences. However, we encourage some flexibility whenever possible. Nature ultimately decides what each litter gives us, and very specific combinations of gender, coat length, color, and shade can significantly increase your wait. Females are generally in higher demand, and our cats also tend to produce fewer females than males. Because of this, families specifically waiting for a female should generally expect a longer wait. Our primary focus is British Longhairs, with British Shorthairs available more occasionally. We primarily produce golden varieties, including black golden shaded and chinchilla, blue golden, and occasionally other golden variations.

Can you help me choose a kitten based on personality?

Absolutely! This is actually one of our favorite parts. I've been known to become a bit of a kitty matchmaker! As kittens grow, we spend a lot of time observing their personalities, including who is especially confident, calm, playful, independent, people-oriented, adventurous, cuddly, or somewhere in between. While kitten personalities are still developing and we can never guarantee exactly what an adult cat will be like, we're happy to share what we're seeing and help guide you toward a kitten who may complement your household.

Can I meet the kittens, call, or FaceTime before reserving?

Occasionally! We do make exceptions for in-person meetings or phone calls when time and circumstances allow, but unfortunately aren't able to guarantee them for every inquiry. Astrid Moon is a home-based cattery, and caring for our cats and kittens remains our first priority. With the volume of inquiries we receive, we're unable to accommodate a call or visit for every prospective family. We prefer to keep all kitten inquiries together through email so conversations, preferences, and important information aren't spread across several different platforms. Due to social media policies, we are also unable to provide certain reservation, availability, or waitlist information through social media.

What health testing do you perform?

The health of our cats and kittens is incredibly important to us. Our breeding cats receive genetic testing through Basepaws' genetic screening panel and are negative for FIV and FeLV. We also perform regular PCR testing within our cattery as part of our ongoing health-monitoring practices. This allows us to stay proactive and quickly identify potential infectious concerns that can naturally arise in a multi-cat environment. It's also important to understand that genetic screening has limitations. Not every hereditary condition can currently be identified through a genetic test, and some conditions may be polygenic, meaning multiple genes and other factors can contribute to their development. For this reason, we don't rely on genetic testing alone. We continually monitor the health of the cats and kittens we produce. If we identify a health concern that may have a hereditary component, the affected breeding cat or related breeding pair may be retired from our breeding program.

Do you offer a health guarantee?

Yes. Every Astrid Moon kitten is covered by our three-year congenital and hereditary health guarantee, as outlined in our sales agreement. We also require new families to establish care with their own veterinarian shortly after pickup so their kitten can continue receiving appropriate veterinary care.

What veterinary care and vaccinations will my kitten receive?

Before going home, kittens receive age-appropriate FVRCP vaccinations, veterinary examinations, and routine parasite evaluation and/or prevention as appropriate. Our kittens are evaluated to make sure they are developing appropriately and are ready to transition into their new homes. You will receive your kitten's available health and vaccination records so your veterinarian can continue their vaccination and wellness schedule.

At what age can my kitten go home?

Our kittens generally begin going home at approximately 12 weeks of age or later, depending on the individual kitten. We don't base readiness on age alone. Development, weight, veterinary care, vaccination timing, and the kitten's overall readiness are all considered before we send a baby home. Occasionally, we may recommend keeping a kitten with us a little longer if we feel they would benefit from additional time.

Are kittens spayed or neutered before going home?

Our kittens go home unaltered, allowing them additional time to grow and develop before being spayed or neutered. Pet families are responsible for completing the required spay/neuter according to the terms of our sales agreement. Unless specifically agreed upon in advance, our kittens are placed as pets rather than for breeding.

Where are you located, and how does pickup work?

Astrid Moon Cattery is located in the Lake Travis area outside of Austin, Texas. Pickup arrangements are coordinated individually with each family. Depending on scheduling, we may arrange pickup locally or meet families at a mutually convenient location in the Austin area. For families flying into Texas, meeting at or around Austin-Bergstrom International Airport may also be possible.

Do you work with families outside of Texas or offer delivery?

Absolutely! We work with families outside of Texas, and distance doesn't necessarily prevent you from bringing home an Astrid Moon kitten. Families are welcome to fly or drive to Texas for pickup. Depending on availability, we can also discuss personal delivery. Personal delivery costs are separate from the kitten's purchase price and include the cost of round-trip airfare, the airline's in-cabin pet fee, and a personal delivery fee based on the travel required. Travel expenses are due when flights are booked. Families are also welcome to coordinate transportation through a pet transportation company of their choice. If a third-party transporter will be picking up your kitten, all remaining balances and other outstanding amounts must be paid in full before the kitten is released into the transporter's care. For international families, the buyer is responsible for researching and coordinating transportation, import requirements, documentation, and any other requirements for bringing a kitten into their country.

What are British Longhairs and British Shorthairs like?

British Longhairs and British Shorthairs are known for their sweet, easygoing personalities and signature teddy-bear appearance. The primary difference between the two is coat length, while their general breed temperament is very similar. British cats tend to be calm, moderately playful, confident, and relatively independent. Many enjoy being close to their people without requiring constant attention. Personality can vary tremendously from kitten to kitten, and we've produced everything from classic independent British personalities to incredibly affectionate little velcro kittens who want to follow their people everywhere.

When do you decide to retire a breeding cat?

There are many reasons we may choose to retire a cat from our breeding program, and sometimes that decision is made much earlier than originally anticipated. A breeding cat may be retired if they do not thrive in a multi-cat environment, demonstrate a weaker immune system, do not meet our health-screening expectations, or develop a health concern that makes continued breeding inappropriate. We also carefully evaluate what our cats produce. If we see a concerning pattern among offspring that could have a hereditary or polygenic component, we may retire one or both parents. Temperament is equally important, and consistently skittish temperaments in a breeding cat or the kittens they produce can also influence our decision. We generally do not keep our studs in active breeding beyond approximately 3–4 years of age, and our females are retired no later than 5 years of age. Females are also limited to a maximum of four litters during their time in our breeding program.

How are your kittens raised and socialized?

Our kittens are raised in our home and grow up as part of our everyday environment rather than in an isolated setting. From a young age, they're exposed to normal household activity, human interaction, handling, play, and the sights and sounds of daily life. As they grow, we spend a lot of time observing how each kitten responds to people, new experiences, and their environment. This not only helps with socialization but also allows us to get to know each kitten individually so we can better guide families when it comes time to choose their kitten.

How do I inquire about a kitten or join the waitlist?

If you’re interested in one of our kittens, would like to join our waitlist, or simply have a question, you can get in touch with us in one of two ways:

Complete our Kitten Application — If you’re actively looking for a kitten, this is the best place to start. The application gives us the information we need about your preferences, timeframe, and what you’re looking for so we can better assist you with availability and approximate wait times.

Email us directly — If you have a general question or aren’t quite ready to complete an application, you’re always welcome to email us.

You do not need to do both. Either option will begin your inquiry with us.

Please note that all follow-up communication is handled through email. Due to social media policies and our preference to keep inquiries organized in one place, we are unable to manage pricing, availability, reservations, or waitlist inquiries through social media.

What payment methods do you accept?

We do not accept credit cards.

Our $800 non-refundable reservation deposit can be paid through Zelle or Venmo and is applied toward the total purchase price of your kitten.

The remaining balance can be paid by cash, Zelle, or Venmo and is due according to the terms outlined in our sales agreement.

Please note that a kitten is not considered officially reserved until the required reservation deposit has been received.
